Let’s dive into Chapter 9: Sustaining Change—Keeping the Momentum Alive.
You know, the real test of any change isn’t just whether you can start it, but whether you can actually make it stick. It’s easy to ride the wave of excitement at the beginning, but what happens when the novelty fades? That’s when the true challenge begins—finding ways to keep that momentum going, day after day.
Lasting change needs your ongoing attention. It’s about gentle reinforcement—little reminders and check-ins that keep your goals from slipping quietly into the background. If you’re not careful, old habits or new distractions can sneak in and take over.
So, how do you keep your new habits alive? One of the best ways is to build in regular check-ins or rituals. Maybe it’s a weekly team meeting where everyone shares progress, a monthly moment to reflect on your personal goals, or even an annual celebration of how far you’ve come. These aren’t just formalities—they’re opportunities to pause, look back, and recommit to the journey.
There’s something else that really helps—going back to your “why.” Over time, that original burst of motivation can fade, especially if the results don’t show up right away. So, take a moment to reconnect with what really matters. Is it better health? A stronger team? Or maybe, creating a more innovative culture? When you remember your deeper purpose, it gives your motivation a fresh boost.
Here are a few simple ways to keep change alive in your life:
First, schedule regular reviews. Set aside a little time to look at what’s working, what’s not, and what you might want to tweak.
Next, refresh your motivation. Revisit the stories, images, or experiences that first inspired you. Sometimes, all it takes is a single memory or success story to light that spark again.
And finally, be willing to adapt. Life changes, so your goals and routines might need to shift too. Don’t be afraid to adjust as new circumstances come up.
Let’s look at a couple of real-world examples. Imagine a company that’s made customer service a priority. To keep their team inspired, they share new customer success stories every quarter. Or think about someone who’s built a meditation habit—they might join a retreat, or try out a new practice to keep things fresh and deepen their commitment.
In the end, sustaining change isn’t about harsh discipline—it’s more about gentle, ongoing care. When you tend to your goals with patience and a bit of flexibility, that new way of doing things gradually becomes part of who you are, or part of your team’s culture.
So, keep the momentum alive. Change doesn’t just happen once; it’s something you nurture, one day at a time.
